title: Customer-level usage normalization and chargeback pipeline
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a resilient, auditable pipeline to normalize raw token events from multiple ingestion sources into a single per-customer chargeable ledger. This ticket covers ingestion normalization, timezone and currency alignment, handling partial streaming tokens, KV-cache credits, and producing daily chargeback snapshots usable by billing and finance. Goal: eliminate current discrepancies between console usage UI, internal billing reports, and invoices for customers on Dedicated and Hosted plans.
acceptance_criteria: A1: End-to-end nightly job produces a per-customer ledger table with total billable tokens and cost metadata for prior-day (P-1) with <0.5% divergence vs reference sampler
A2: Reconciliation job can trace any aggregated entry back to source events and original request IDs for audit within 48 hours
A3: Streaming/partial-response cases (client disconnects / connection resets) are accounted deterministically and not double-billed
A4: KV cache hit credits and batching discounts are applied according to policy and visible as separate line items
A5: Test harness (local + CI) validating at least three edge cases: clock skew, duplicate events, and late-arriving records
implementation_plan: 1) Ingest: unify events from streaming ledger (kafka-topics/stream-tokens), batching service logs, and offline aggregation into a canonical Avro schema with canonical request_id and customer_id fields
2) Normalization: windowed deduplication keyed by request_id + idempotency_token, timezone canonicalization to UTC, and sequence_length heuristics to split sessions into billable spans
3) Cost mapping: apply model-version pricing table and per-customer override rules; include fields for effective_price_per_token, kv_cache_credit, batching_discount_percent
4) Reconciliation: a daily MapReduce-style job to produce chargeback snapshots and a near-real-time materialized view for console metrics
5) Backfill: implement windowed backfill with safe checkpoints and tombstone handling for late-arriving data
6) Expose: materialize results to BigQuery (or equivalent) table used by billing microservice and Console dashboards
progress_updates: 2026-01-22: Kickoff meeting with Billing, Console, and Serving runtime teams. Agreed canonical schema and list of source topics.
2026-01-28: Draft Avro schema posted in shared drive and validated against sample streams. Noted missing idempotency_token on several legacy events; added retrofitting plan.
2026-02-05: Prototyped deduplication layer using Beam job; duplicate rate reduced by 87% in synthetic tests. Observed edge-case with partial streams from mobile SDK.
2026-02-12: Implemented first pass of KV cache credit logic in test stage; needs review from Runtime team on credit calculation when caching TTLs vary by model.
2026-02-20: Reconciliation harness completed for P-1 snapshot; initial comparison against finance reference shows 1.9% delta — next step is investigate batching attribution logic.
risks: R1: Late-arriving events could shift daily totals and complicate invoice stability; mitigation: define SLA window for invoice-finalization and mark adjustments as credits

R2: Differences between hosted and dedicated routing (model variant fallbacks) may produce inconsistent model_version metadata; mitigation: add model_family and compatibility mapping during normalization
R3: Performance: realtime materialized views may be costly to maintain at high throughput; mitigation: throttle real-time materialization and rely on nightly authoritative snapshot for billing
R4: Security: event payloads contain PII in some integrations; mitigation: strip or hash sensitive fields during ingestion and require security review before enabling for Private deployments
qa_plan: Unit tests for dedup and timezone-canonicalization
Integration test harness replaying sampled production traffic (anonymized) to verify end-to-end totals
Fuzz tests for partial-streamed responses and connection resets
Acceptance test validating traceability from chargeback entry to original request_id
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Run normalization job in parallel for 7 days and compare outputs with current billing pipeline for a set of 25 pilot customers
Phase 2 (Opt-in): Allow finance to consume consolidated snapshots for invoicing of non-enterprise accounts; collect feedback and adjust crediting rules
Phase 3 (Cutover): Switch billing microservice to authoritative normalized table and deprecate legacy aggregator after a week-long overlap
Rollback: Keep legacy snapshots for 30 days and provide an automated diff tool to revert if divergence > 2%
